transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having trouble staying with things at work. Like, I’ll start an EPIC quality report or be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I really mean to follow it… but after a few minutes I realize my mind’s gone somewhere else. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or I’ve missed the main point of what was said. That’s what finally made me think I should talk to someone.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yes… I think so. In elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright but careless. My mom had to sit with me to get homework done because I’d lose track of assignments or forget books at school.
Outside of work, do you also have the same trouble staying focused?

Yes, it can happen outside of work too, but… the place I notice it most is work. Like with EPIC reports or clinic metrics meetings, I’ll sit down meaning to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize I’m rereading the same numbers or I missed what people were actually talking about.
Do you often feel restless or like you need to keep moving, even when you’re supposed to sit still?
Not really… I don’t think of myself as needing to move around all the time. I can sit still when I have to.
Do you often find that worry makes it hard for you to concentrate?
I’m not sure. I mean, I worry sometimes like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed that being the main thing that makes it hard to concentrate.
Have these attention problems caused significant trouble for you in your home life?

Some, yes. I mean… home life maybe less than work, but it spills over. I’ve fallen behind on clinic reporting deadlines, and then other teams are waiting on me. And I’ve had to pull back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I can’t always keep the planning pieces moving reliably.
During times when your mood is normal, do you still have the same trouble paying attention?

Yes. Even when my mood is fine, it still happens. I’ll sit down to do an EPIC quality report or be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I’m trying to follow along… but a few minutes later I realize I’ve drifted and I’m rereading the same numbers, or I missed the point of what was just discussed.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping track of what needs to get done?

Yes… I do. If I’m given, say, three or four follow-up things after a committee meeting, I’ll usually do the first one, maybe start the second. But then something like the email or spreadsheet or final submission just… sits there until someone reminds me.
Do you also lose focus during activities you actually enjoy?

Yes… it can happen even when I’m interested. Like with an EPIC quality report or a clinic metrics meeting, I’ll start out really intending to follow it, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve drifted. I’m rereading the same numbers or I’ve missed the main point of what was being discussed.
Do you often lose things you need for work or daily life?

Yes… I do. I’m always misplacing things like my badge, handwritten notes, clinic folders… even a flash drive I just had right before a meeting. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I used to be the organized one.
Do you often forget everyday tasks, like returning calls, paying bills, or showing up to appointments?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t think that’s the main issue for me. I haven’t noticed a lot of missed appointments or unpaid bills, at least not in a way I can clearly point to.
Do you tend to procrastinate starting tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort?

Yes… I do. Especially with things like dense policy reviews or long blocks of data analysis. I’ll put them off until later in the day because just starting feels… harder than it should, like it takes a lot to make myself sit with that much detail.
Have you been feeling down or depressed كثيرًا lately?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I’ve been frustrated, but I wouldn’t say depressed a lot.
Did these concentration problems start after a particularly stressful event in your life?
Not exactly a stressful event. It was more… after I got promoted, about two years and a few months ago. The bigger portfolio just started to overwhelm the systems I used to rely on.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about different parts of your life?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive. I worry about things sometimes, like anyone, but… I don’t think that’s the main issue for me.
Do you often feel physically tense or unable to relax, even when there isn’t an obvious reason?
Not really… I mean, I get tired or keyed up sometimes, but I haven’t noticed being physically tense for no reason.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood across more than one setting, with clear occupational impairment. Confirmed symptoms include distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, disorganization, losing necessary items, and procrastination/avoidance of tasks requiring sustained mental effort. Hyperactivity is denied, supporting a predominantly inattentive ADHD presentation. Anxiety, depression, mood-state dependence, and a discrete stress-related onset were not supported as primary explanations.
